name: CS50: Introduction to Computer Science (Harvard/edX)
note: The single most-recommended CS intro course online. Great for building real fundamentals before/alongside a college curriculum.

name: freeCodeCamp
note: Full curriculum with certifications in web dev, Python, data analysis, and more. Great for building projects while learning.

name: The Odin Project
note: Project-based full-stack web development path (HTML/CSS/JS, Ruby or Node).

name: LeetCode
note: Practice data structures & algorithms questions used in technical interviews.

name: NeetCode
note: Curated, structured roadmap through the most important LeetCode-style problems with video explanations.

name: Visualgo
note: Visualizations of data structures and algorithms — very useful for building intuition.

name: MIT OpenCourseWare
note: Full MIT course materials, including 6.006 (Algorithms) and 6.042 (Math for CS).

name: Git & GitHub docs
note: Version control is not optional. Learn it early — most students skip this and regret it.

name: Missing Semester (MIT)
note: The practical 'how to actually use a computer' class covering shell, git, debugging, and more — the stuff CS classes assume you already know.

name: roadmap.sh
note: Community-maintained learning roadmaps for frontend, backend, DevOps, and more.

name: Teach Yourself CS
note: Opinionated reading list covering the core topics a CS degree is supposed to give you, with book/course recommendations per topic.

name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
note: Free access to dozens of developer tools, cloud credits, and services while you're a student.

name: Exercism
note: Language-specific coding exercises with mentor feedback across 60+ languages.

name: Pramp / interviewing.io
note: Practice live mock technical interviews with real engineers.

name: Overleaf
note: Online LaTeX editor — useful for CS/math coursework and papers without installing a LaTeX toolchain.
